title: Tier and module-split the smoke suite so a change only runs the tests it can affect
goal: Restructure the smoke suite so that not every change pays for the full browser regression: split the 3709-line system-pages.spec.ts monolith into per-business-module specs, introduce explicit L0/L1/L2/L3 tiers, and drive module selection from the changed paths so the PR gate runs the critical path plus only the touched modules. No assertion, route, permission string or fixture may change.
findings: The PR-blocking smoke job (quality.yml `smoke-sanity`) ran `npm run test:smoke:platform:contracts && npm run test:smoke:system:pages`, i.e. 2 contract specs plus one 3709-line / 81-test monolith, on every pull request regardless of what changed.
A single file carried 59 of the 81 tests, spanning six unrelated business modules (iam, config, i18n, audit, org, platform). Any change anywhere in the system domain re-ran all six.
There was no tier between 'static contract' and 'full browser regression': the only fast signal was the pre-build contract gates, and the only browser signal was the monolith.

The monolith also hid a verification gap: `frontend/tests/**` is covered by neither `tsc` (tsconfig.app.json includes only `src`) nor the CI eslint step (`eslint src`). The split needed a type-check of its own to be verifiable.
Module selection must fail safe: a shared-core or wiring change has to escalate to every module, otherwise a split would silently reduce coverage instead of re-focusing it.
smoke-core is deliberately report-only (README: '转 blocking 需在连续多轮全绿后按 harness 规则切换'), so the new L1 tier must not absorb it.

in: frontend/package.json (per-module scripts, L0/L1/L2 tiers, module:<name> entries)
frontend/tests/smoke/README.md (script entry map, coverage matrix, test tier documentation)
frontend/config/system-page-admission.json (repoint requiredSmokeAssertions at the new spec file)
.github/workflows/quality.yml (change-scope exposes the module list; smoke-sanity becomes L1; new blocking pr-smoke-modules job)
out: Any change to a test assertion, expectation, route string, permission string, fixture value or cleanup step
Any production source change: no frontend/src or backend/ source file is modified
Making smoke-core blocking: it stays report-only per tests/smoke-core/README.md until it has been green for several consecutive runs
Splitting the five platform/system-secondary-route-*.spec.ts files or backoffice-ui-visual.spec.ts
Adding a type-check of tests/ to CI: doing so would surface 69 pre-existing errors unrelated to this change (recorded as a follow-up)

acceptanceCriteria: The split is provably behaviour-preserving: every one of the 59 top-level test blocks is byte-identical to its pre-split form and the multiset of blocks is unchanged.
All 81 runtime tests survive: 59 literal blocks plus the 14-entry systemPages loop, the 4-entry workspacePages loop and the 4 registrar tests.
The shared helper region is preserved line-for-line (845 lines), with only an `export` prefix added to declaration lines.
The split introduces no new TypeScript error and removes none: the before/after error-message multiset is identical.
eslint passes on tests/ with zero warnings (no unused imports from the generated import lists).
All 13 pre-build contract gates pass, including check:smoke-coverage-contract (34 smoke specs, 20 script entries) and check:system-page-admission (16 entries).
scripts/resolve-smoke-modules.mjs resolves unambiguous module paths to that module, and escalates every shared/unknown path to all modules; its unit test passes.
The new pr-smoke-modules job is wired into the Quality Gates aggregator so it blocks when it runs, and is skipped (not failed) when no module is touched.

commands: cd frontend && npx tsc -p tsconfig.spec-check.json --noEmit (before/after error-set diff)
cd frontend && npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm run prebuild
runtimeEvidence: before/after TypeScript error multiset diff (69 = 69, 0 new, 0 gone)
parsed quality.yml job graph showing the new job and the aggregator wiring

runtimeGap: Playwright cannot execute on this host (Node cannot spawn child processes: spawnSync fails with EBUSY), so the split specs are not run locally. The change is verified locally by byte-level equivalence against the pre-split file plus eslint/tsc/prebuild; the executed proof comes from CI, where the blocking Quality Gates jobs run the L1 and module suites against a real backend.
